Definition: to pound the earth (as a sign of passion); by analogy to expand (by hammering); by implication, to overlay (with thin sheets of metal)
BiblicalUsage: Raqa' is to pound out, to beat thin, to stamp — by analogy, to spread out by hammering, and to overlay with thin sheets of metal. The workmen beat the gold into thin plates and cut it into wires to work into the blue and purple; the workman melteth a graven image, and the goldsmith spreadeth it over with gold; and David says, 'Then did I beat them as small as the dust of the earth, I did stamp them as the mire of the street.'
TheologicalSignificance: What I see here is that the hammer falls on gold and on enemies alike: the same beating that makes the ephod beautiful makes the wicked as dust — and the difference is whose hand holds the hammer.
